node_definition: MRCA(Romanian, Italian, French, Spanish, ...): Eastern Romance + Italo-Western Romance
event: Aurelian's withdrawal of Roman troops/administration from Dacia south of the Danube, 271 CE (Watson 1999)
bound_type: point (as published); better treated as max-leaning soft interval
suggested_distribution: Normal(mu=1679, sd=150) or Uniform(1450,1900) soft; Normal(mu=1679, sd=383) [Maurits2020 rule of thumb: 95% in 929-2429]
notes: Holman2011: 1729 BP (H), present=2000 | Serva&Petroni2008 calibrate Italian-French separation = 1600 y; Bouckaert2012 calibrate a different node (Latin+Romance, see IE-LATROM-01) | Assumes Daco-Romanian continuity north of the Danube after 271 CE; the continuity vs. later-immigration debate means Eastern Romance may have separated from Balkan Latin later (6th-7th c.). Also Latin continued as a written koine long after 271, so the date is an event, not a measured split. Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.
source_original: Watson A. 1999. Aurelian and the Third Century (as cited in Holman2011)

node_definition: MRCA(Italo-Dalmatian, Western Romance: Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan...)
event: Deposition of Romulus Augustulus, 476 CE ('fall' of Western Roman Empire; Bury 1923)
suggested_distribution: Normal(mu=1474, sd=383) [Maurits2020 rule of thumb: 95% in 724-2224]
notes: Holman2011: 1524 BP (H) | Political event used as proxy for linguistic divergence; no direct linguistic evidence. Holman et al. themselves note Bury argued against 476 as a real break. Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.
source_original: Bury JB. 1923. History of the Later Roman Empire (as cited in Holman2011)

node_definition: MRCA(North Germanic, West Germanic) [Holman: Gothic not in ASJP comparison]
event: Appearance of Cimbri and Teutones, late 2nd c. BCE, taken as start of Germanic migrations (Pohl 2004)

notes: Holman2011: 2100 BP (H) | Ethnic identification of Cimbri/Teutones as Germanic speakers is itself debated; the node in Holman is effectively Northwest Germanic (no Gothic). Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.

node_definition: MRCA(North Germanic, West Germanic incl. Old English, OHG, Old Norse)

suggested_distribution: Per Maurits2020: an inscription in a daughter gives only a MIN bound on the parent split; use offset/one-sided e.g. min 1700 BP soft, no informative max
notes: Bouckaert2012: normalPrior(mean=1875, stdev=67) on tmrca(Northwest-Germanic) | Explicitly criticised by Maurits2020: an inscription in a descendant language cannot by itself narrowly date the parent's disintegration; the implied 30-300 yr gap is unstated.
source_original: Bouckaert2012 SI; critique in Maurits2020

source_original: Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok tradition; standard historiography)

notes: Gray 2010 (PLoS ONE) excluded it from the 'robust' set as contestable (red-slipped pottery = Austronesian arrival). Cochrane et al. 2021 model initial pottery in N Luzon at 5430-4290 cal BP (Nagsabaran 5440-4270), older than this range; Batan Island charcoal-only 3380-2590 cal BP. Gray 2009 reports root age barely changed (5230 vs 5230) without this constraint. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.

Using Gray 2009 range inflates Polynesian ages. Retain only for replicating Gray 2009. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Kirch PV, Green RC 2001 Hawaiki, Ancestral Polynesia (CUP); Green RC 2003 (as cited in Gray 2009 SOM)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3) 10.1126/science.1166858

event: Earliest settlement of East Polynesia: Society Islands AD c. 1025-1120 (short-lived samples), i.e. 925-830 BP
notes: Maximum for EP diversification under the short chronology. Some argue for earlier occupation (e.g. Hawaii AD 940-1130, Athens et al. 2014), which would push the bound to c. 1010 BP; Gambier 1108-1275 ambiguous.
source_original: Wilmshurst JM, Hunt TL, Lipo CP, Anderson AJ 2011 PNAS 108(5):1815-1820 10.1073/pnas.1015876108

node_definition: MRCA of Rapanui and Central-Eastern Polynesian
event: Settlement of Rapa Nui AD c. 1200-1253 (Wilmshurst 2011); c. AD 1200 (Hunt & Lipo 2006) -> Rapanui lineage separated no later than this
notes: Requires Rapanui to be the first offshoot of EP (standard subgrouping) and no later re-contact. Combined with AN-014 brackets PEP at c. 700-930 BP.
source_original: Hunt TL, Lipo CP 2006 Science 311:1603-1606; Wilmshurst JM, Hunt TL, Lipo CP, Anderson AJ 2011 PNAS 108(5):1815-1820 10.1126/science.1121879; 10.1073/pnas.1015876108

node_definition: Split of Hawaiian from closest EP relatives (Marquesan, Mangarevan)
event: Settlement of Hawaii: AD c. 1219-1266 (Wilmshurst 2011) vs AD 940-1130 (95% HPD; Athens, Rieth & Dye 2014)
notes: Two chronologies differ by 100-300 y. Hawaiian may have had later Tahitian contact (traditions; lexical borrowing), so split may be younger than settlement - weak minimum.
source_original: Wilmshurst JM, Hunt TL, Lipo CP, Anderson AJ 2011 PNAS 108(5):1815-1820; Athens JS, Rieth TM, Dye TS 2014 American Antiquity 79(1):144-155 10.1073/pnas.1015876108; 10.7183/0002-7316.79.1.144

node_definition: Split of New Zealand Maori from Cook Islands Maori/Tahitian
event: Settlement of New Zealand AD c. 1230-1282 (Wilmshurst 2011); rat-gnawed seeds/bones post-date c. AD 1280 (Wilmshurst et al. 2008)
notes: Robust settlement date; as a language split it assumes no post-settlement contact (voyaging to/from NZ probably continued briefly). Also a maximum for Maori dialect diversification.
source_original: Wilmshurst JM, Hunt TL, Lipo CP, Anderson AJ 2011 PNAS 108(5):1815-1820; Wilmshurst JM et al. 2008 PNAS 105(22):7676-7680 10.1073/pnas.1015876108; 10.1073/pnas.0801507105

node_definition: Split of Moriori (Chatham Is.) from NZ Maori
event: Settlement of Rekohu (Chatham Islands): earliest reliable 14C on kopi seed cal AD 1450-1620 (95%); commonly cited c. AD 1500. Maximum is NZ settlement (c. AD 1280)
notes: Traditions, Moriori-Maori dialect differences and archaic artefacts have been argued to indicate 13th-c. settlement; radiocarbon supports 15th-16th c. Moriori assumed derived from NZ Maori; Moriori data are sparse 19th-c. records.
source_original: Barber IG, Maxwell JJ, Petchey F 2016 J Archaeol Sci Reports 10:96-109 10.1016/j.jasrep.2016.08.040

node_definition: Settlement of the Marquesas (min for Marquesic lineage split from Tahitic)
event: Settlement of the Marquesas AD 1200-1277
notes: Earlier claims of Marquesan settlement c. 2000 BP (long chronology) are rejected by Wilmshurst 2011.
source_original: Wilmshurst JM, Hunt TL, Lipo CP, Anderson AJ 2011 PNAS 108(5):1815-1820 10.1073/pnas.1015876108

node_definition: MRCA of Nuclear Micronesian languages (Chuukic, Pohnpeic, Kosraean, Marshallese, Kiribati)
event: Settlement of (eastern) Micronesia 1900-2200 BP (Gray 2009, after Pawley 2002); Greenhill 2017 Normal(2000,100)
notes: Atoll settlement after mid-Holocene highstand; Micronesian diversification probably post-dates arrival. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Pawley A 2002 (see AN-003)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); Greenhill SJ et al. 2017 PNAS (Evolutionary dynamics of language systems; normal priors) 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1073/pnas.1700388114

node_definition: Split of Chamorro from its closest Malayo-Polynesian relatives (Philippine/Western MP)
event: Initial settlement of the Mariana Islands c. 1500 BC (Carson; earliest Unai Bapot ranges 1916-1558 cal BC, preferred 1612-1558 BC)
notes: Rieth & Athens 2017/2019 Bayesian model argue for a later (Lapita-contemporaneous) Marianas settlement - exact range not verified here. Chamorro has a later Philippine/Latte-period overlay; linguistic link of first settlers uncertain (aDNA Pugach et al. 2021 PNAS links to Philippines). Min = split no later than settlement only if Chamorro descends from first settlers.

node_definition: MRCA of Chamic languages (Cham, Jarai, Rade, Roglai, Tsat; excl. Acehnese)
event: Chamic speakers described in Chinese records c. 1800 BP and probable entry into Vietnam c. 2600 BP: Gray 2009 range 1800-2500 BP (after Thurgood 1999)
notes: Maurits et al. 2020 criticise this: Chinese records attest the polity (Linyi/Champa), not a unified Proto-Chamic language, so the bound is unjustified. Also note Gray 2010 listed Chamic among calibrations dropped from the robust set. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Thurgood G 1999 From Ancient Cham to Modern Dialects (Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 28, Univ. Hawai'i Press)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); critique: Maurits L et al. 2020 J Lang Evol 5(1):17-38 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1093/jole/lzz009

node_definition: MRCA of Malayic and Chamic (incl. Acehnese)
event: Existence of Malayo-Chamic subgroup 2000-3000 BP (Gray 2009, after Thurgood 1999)
notes: Burstclock maps to 'North and East Malayo-Sumbawan' (nort3170, not in current Glottolog); current Glottolog node is Malayo-Chamic mala1554. Inferential, weakly justified. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Thurgood G 1999 (as AN-022)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3) 10.1126/science.1166858

node_definition: Old Cham, earliest attested Chamic language
event: Dong Yen Chau inscription (near Tra Kieu, Vietnam), undated but late 4th c. AD by match with dated Sanskrit inscriptions of Bhadravarman I; widely cited as the oldest text in any Austronesian language
notes: Dating is paleographic/contextual, not absolute; text is short. Also implies Chamic lineage (and possibly Proto-Chamic) older than c. 1600 BP. Thurgood regards the Tra Kieu-area inscription as the earliest Austronesian document. Glottocode for Old Cham not verified.
source_original: Coedès G 1939 (BEFEO 39); Thurgood G 1999

event: Kedukan Bukit inscription (Palembang), Saka 604/605 = AD 682/683; earliest dated Old Malay text
notes: Year reading Saka 604 vs 605 (AD 682 vs 683) differs between sources; immaterial. Other Srivijaya inscriptions (Talang Tuwo 684, Kota Kapur 686) corroborate.
source_original: Coedès G 1930 BEFEO 30 (Les inscriptions malaises de Çrivijaya)

event: Old Javanese as spoken/written 700-1200 BP (Gray 2009 tip calibration, after Zoetmulder 1982); earliest wholly Javanese inscription Sukabumi, 25 March AD 804 (1146 BP)
notes: One of Gray 2010's five robust calibrations. Literary Old Javanese corpus spans 9th-15th c.; choose range matching the lexical source used (Zoetmulder dictionary = mostly 10th-14th c. literature). Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Zoetmulder PJ 1982 Old Javanese-English Dictionary (KITLV)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); Greenhill, Drummond & Gray 2010 PLoS ONE 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1371/journal.pone.0009573

event: Proto-Javanese 1100-1300 BP (Gray 2009 Table S3, after Zoetmulder 1982 and Anderson & Sinoto 2002 as cited)
notes: Justification thin: Old Javanese texts imply Javanese lineage existed by then; making it the MRCA of modern Javanese varieties assumes those varieties diverged after Old Javanese. Inconsistent with treating Old Javanese (700-1200) as a descendant tip. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Zoetmulder 1982
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3) 10.1126/science.1166858

event: Settlement of Madagascar 1100-1300 BP (Gray 2009, after Verin & Wright 1999); Asian crops (rice, mung bean, cotton) dominate Madagascar/Comoros sites from c. AD 700-900 (Crowther et al. 2016)
notes: Settlement is logically a maximum for Malagasy dialect diversification, not a node age. Serva et al. 2012 (lexicostatistics) date Indonesian colonisation c. AD 650. Earlier forager presence (Dewar et al. 2013) irrelevant to the Austronesian arrival. Gray 2009 Table S3 ages are 'years before present' as published (not explicitly 1950-based; Favorlang/Siraya 346-384 implies a c. 2000-2010 basis, so subtract c. 50-60 y for 1950 basis). Values reproduced via Kaiping et al. burstclock supplement (github Anaphory/burstclock add_calibrations.py) because Science SOM was not retrievable; treat exact numbers as verified-secondary.
source_original: Verin P, Wright H 1999 (as cited in Gray 2009 SOM; full reference not verified); Crowther A et al. 2016 PNAS 113(24):6635-6640 10.1073/pnas.1522714113 (Crowther 2016 only)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); Serva M, Petroni F, Volchenkov D, Wichmann S 2012 J R Soc Interface 9(66):54-67 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1098/rsif.2011.0228

event: Malagasy separated from Ma'anyan no later than the Austronesian settlement of Madagascar (crops AD 700-900; Serva 2012 c. AD 650)
notes: Assumes Malagasy migrants left Borneo after the Malagasy-Ma'anyan split began (Dahl 1951; Adelaar). Adelaar argues migration was led by Malay speakers from Sumatra (Malay/Javanese loans), so departure may post-date the split substantially.
source_dating_study: Serva M et al. 2012 J R Soc Interface 9:54-67 10.1098/rsif.2011.0228

event: Happart's Favorlang dictionary manuscript, 1650 (Gray 2009 used 346-384 BP 'age of source data')
notes: Gray et al. 2010 robust set. Burstclock excluded Favorlang because ABVD data mix mid-1600s Dutch sources with c. 1900 wordlists - check the source of each item before using.
source_original: Happart G 1650 (ms; publ. Medhurst 1840, Campbell 1896)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); Greenhill et al. 2010 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1371/journal.pone.0009573

event: Gravius' Siraya Gospels of Matthew and John (Amsterdam 1661) and Catechism (1662); Gray 2009 used 346-384 BP
notes: Gray et al. 2010 robust set. 1950-basis ages here computed from 1661-1662; Gray's 346-384 BP is on a present (c. 2000s) basis.
source_original: Gravius D 1661 Het Heylige Euangelium Matthei en Johannis (Amsterdam)
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3); Greenhill et al. 2010 10.1126/science.1166858; 10.1371/journal.pone.0009573

event: Frederick de Houtman, Spraeck ende Woord-boeck inde Maleysche ende Madagaskarsche Talen, Amsterdam 1603 (Dutch-Malagasy vocabulary)
notes: Small vocabulary; dialect not Plateau Malagasy (plat1254). Useful only if a 1603 Malagasy wordlist is included as a tip.
source_original: de Houtman F 1603 (Amsterdam); Glottolog reference 18058

event: Doctrina Christiana en lengua espanola y tagala, Manila 1593 (first book printed in the Philippines)
notes: Date well established; lexical content limited (religious text). Not independently re-verified via web in this session.
source_original: Doctrina Christiana 1593 (Manila)

event: San Vitores, Gramatica y Doctrina Christiana de la Lengua Mariana, 1668
notes: Date and title from memory; not verified in this session.
source_original: San Vitores DL 1668

node_definition: Arrival of pottery-using (presumed MP-speaking) groups in Sulawesi (Minanga Sipakko)
event: Initial pottery Sulawesi island-wide 4550-3590 cal BP; Minanga Sipakko 4600-3510 cal BP (95% HPD)
notes: Maximum for diversification of Sulawesi MP subgroups if pottery = Austronesian arrival; association contested (multi-directional Neolithic dispersal argued by the authors).
source_original: Cochrane EE, Rieth TM, Filimoehala D 2021 PLoS ONE 16(6):e0251407 10.1371/journal.pone.0251407

node_definition: Sensitivity benchmark: Austronesian root age on 'robust' calibration subset (Proto-Oceanic, Old Javanese, Old Chinese outgroup, Favorlang, Siraya)
event: Benchmark result: root mean 5117 BP, 95% HPD 4660-5680 BP with five least controversial calibrations (vs 5230, 4750-5800 with full set)
notes: Held-out benchmark, not a calibration. Old Chinese (2300-2900 BP) was used as the Sino-Tibetan outgroup tip in Gray 2009.
source_original: Greenhill SJ, Drummond AJ, Gray RD 2010 PLoS ONE 5(3):e9573 10.1371/journal.pone.0009573
source_dating_study: Gray RD, Drummond AJ, Greenhill SJ 2009 Science 323:479-483 (SOM Table S3) 10.1126/science.1166858

node_definition: MRCA of Inuit varieties east of the Mackenzie delta (Inuinnaqtun, Eastern Canadian Inuktitut, Kalaallisut, Tunumiisut, Inuktun)
event: Thule (ancestral Inuit) expansion from Alaska into the Canadian Arctic; no secure Thule occupation in western Canadian Arctic before 13th c. CE (Friesen & Arnold 2008); Greenland reached c. 1300 CE
notes: Older 'c. 1000 CE' Thule chronology (pre-McGhee 2000) would push the bound to ~950 BP; Raghavan et al. 2014 aDNA consistent with recent Thule spread. Bound applies to the eastern dialect chain only, not to Alaskan Inupiaq.
source_original: Friesen & Arnold 2008, The timing of the Thule migration: new dates from the western Canadian Arctic, American Antiquity 73(3):527-538 10.1017/s0002731600046850
source_dating_study: Raghavan et al. 2014, The genetic prehistory of the New World Arctic, Science 345:1255832 10.1126/science.1255832

node_definition: MRCA of all Inuit languages (Alaskan Inupiaq through Greenlandic)
event: Proto-Inuit = Birnirk/Thule horizon of northern Alaska; ASJP calibration 'Inuit' = 800 years
notes: Holman et al. value (800) is in years before c. 2000 CE, i.e. ~750 BP(1950). Fortescue et al. (CED) put Proto-Inuit at ~1000 years (secondary report, unverified). ASJP estimated 945, GBD 1710 (Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 5) - a held-out benchmark that GBD badly overshoots.
source_original: Holman et al. 2011, Automated dating of the world's language families based on lexical similarity, Current Anthropology 52(6):841-875 (calibration value as tabulated in Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 1) 10.1086/662127
source_dating_study: Rama & Wichmann 2020, A test of Generalized Bayesian dating, PLOS ONE 15(8):e0236522 10.1371/journal.pone.0236522

node_definition: MRCA of Yupik languages (Central Alaskan Yup'ik, Siberian Yupik, Alutiiq) and Inuit; Sirenik placement unresolved
event: Proto-Eskimo split into Yupik and Inuit branches
notes: Alaska Native Language Center states ~1000 years ago; secondary reports attribute ~2000 years to Proto-Eskimo (Fortescue, Jacobson & Kaplan, Comparative Eskimo Dictionary 1994/2010) - exact wording not verified. Old Bering Sea/Norton correlations are often invoked. Treat as weak.
source_original: Fortescue, Jacobson & Kaplan 1994 (2nd ed. 2010), Comparative Eskimo Dictionary with Aleut Cognates, ANLC Fairbanks

event: Proto-Eskimo-Aleut divergence into Aleut and Eskimo
notes: Bergsland 1986 gives 4000-2000 BCE (via Wikipedia, not checked in original); ANLC: 'at least 4,000 years ago'; Berge 2018 (per ICHL26 handout) 6000-4000 BP for Proto-Eskaleut. Palaeo-Eskimo/Neo-Eskimo genetic links (Flegontov et al. 2019 Nature, 10.1038/s41586-019-1251-y) are argued to fit an Eskaleut spread but do not fix the date.
source_original: Bergsland 1986, Comparative Eskimo-Aleut phonology and lexicon, Journal de la Societe Finno-Ougrienne 80:63-137
source_dating_study: Flegontov et al. 2019 (genetic correlate, not a linguistic date) 10.1038/s41586-019-1251-y

event: Poul Egede, Dictionarium Groenlandico-Danico-Latinum (Copenhagen 1750); Grammatica Groenlandica Danico-Latina 1760
notes: Only useful if 18th-c. lexical forms are coded as a separate tip from modern Kalaallisut; orthography pre-Kleinschmidt.
source_original: Egede, P. 1750. Dictionarium Groenlandico-Danico-Latinum. Copenhagen

node_definition: MRCA of Apachean (Navajo nava1243, Western Apache, Chiricahua, Mescalero, Jicarilla, Lipan, Plains Apache) and Northern Athabaskan
event: Coronado expedition meets bison-hunting 'Querechos' on the Southern Plains (1541), generally identified as Apacheans; possible Apachean ancestors at Promontory Caves, Utah, c. 13th c. CE (Ives et al.)
notes: Querechos=Apache identification is standard but not certain; Promontory attribution (Ives, Janetski) is argued, not proven. Hoijer 1956 glottochronology gives relative Athabaskan chronology (numbers not checked here). The split is certainly older than the attestation; upper end of range is a guess bounded by Proto-Athabaskan, not a published figure.
source_original: Hammond & Rey (eds.) Coronado expedition narratives (1540-42); Ives et al. Promontory Caves project (Univ. Alberta)
source_dating_study: Hoijer 1956, The chronology of the Athapaskan languages, IJAL 22(4):219-232 10.1086/464374

node_definition: MRCA of Apachean languages (Navajo, Western Apache, Chiricahua, Mescalero, Jicarilla, Lipan, Plains Apache)
event: Apachean arrival in the Southwest/Southern Plains, usually placed c. 1300-1500 CE; no secure archaeological evidence before c. 1400 in many areas
notes: Arrival dates are disputed (writers 'disagree widely' per NPS Canyon de Chelly history); some Apachean diversification may predate arrival (Plains Apache/Kiowa-Apache is the deepest split), so the bound is weak. Sources cited here are secondary (NPS); primary: Seymour (ed.) 2012 'From the Land of Ever Winter to the American Southwest' (Univ. of Utah Press) - not checked.
source_original: Seymour (ed.) 2012, From the Land of Ever Winter to the American Southwest: Athapaskan Migrations, Mobility, and Ethnogenesis

node_definition: MRCA of Northern Wakashan (Kwak'wala, Heiltsuk, Haisla, Oowekyala) and Southern Wakashan (Nuu-chah-nulth, Ditidaht, Makah)
event: ASJP calibration 'Wakashan' = 2500 years
evidence_type: archaeology/inference (basis in Holman et al. not checked)
notes: Value from Holman et al. 2011 list via Rama & Wichmann 2020; rationale not verified here. ASJP 3626, glottochronology 4070, GBD 2760 (Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 5) - the methods disagree strongly.
source_original: Holman et al. 2011, Automated dating of the world's language families based on lexical similarity, Current Anthropology 52(6):841-875 (calibration value as tabulated in Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 1) 10.1086/662127
source_dating_study: Rama & Wichmann 2020, A test of Generalized Bayesian dating, PLOS ONE 15(8):e0236522 10.1371/journal.pone.0236522

node_definition: MRCA of Algonquian excluding Blackfoot (Cree-Innu, Arapahoan, Cheyenne, Menominee, Core Central, Eastern Algonquian); Blackfoot possibly a sister (Goddard 2015)
event: Proto-Algonquian spoken c. 1000-500 BCE, probably immediately west of Lake Superior
notes: Date is Pentland 1979:329 as reported by Oxford (Routledge handbook chapter); homeland Goddard 1994a. If Blackfoot is included the root must be older. No Bayesian date found.
source_original: Pentland 1979, Algonquian historical phonology (PhD, Univ. of Toronto):329; Goddard 1994a, The west-to-east cline in Algonquian dialectology
source_dating_study: Oxford, W. (forthcoming/2020s) Algonquian, in Routledge Handbook of North American Languages (preprint, Univ. Manitoba)

event: John Eliot's Massachusett Bible (Mamusse Wunneetupanatamwe Up-Biblum God), complete 1663 (NT 1661)
notes: Large corpus; modern reclamation (Wopanaak) is based on it.
source_original: Eliot, J. 1663. Mamusse Wunneetupanatamwe Up-Biblum God. Cambridge, MA

event: William Strachey's Powhatan vocabulary, compiled c. 1610-1612 (plus John Smith 1612)
notes: Small (~1000 entries), English-orthography wordlist. Extinct by 18th c.
source_original: Strachey, W. c.1612. The Historie of Travaile into Virginia Britannia (vocabulary)

event: Vocabularies recorded on Jacques Cartier's second voyage (1535-36), published in the Brief recit (1545)
notes: ~200 words, partly mixed and transcribed by French speakers; Laurentians disappeared by c. 1580. Its distinctness from Huron and Mohawk also implies Northern Iroquoian diversification well before 1535.
source_original: Cartier, J. 1545. Brief recit et succincte narration de la navigation faicte es ysles de Canada

event: Gabriel Sagard, Le Grand Voyage du pays des Hurons with Dictionaire de la langue huronne (Paris 1632); further Jesuit dictionaries later in the century
notes: Glottocode wyan1247 = Huron-Wyandot.
source_original: Sagard, G. 1632. Dictionaire de la langue huronne. Paris

node_definition: MRCA of Cherokee (cher1273) and Northern Iroquoian (Mohawk, Seneca, Oneida, Cayuga, Onondaga, Tuscarora, Wyandot...)
event: Split between Southern (Cherokee) and Northern Iroquoian
notes: Lounsbury 1961 glottochronology 3500-3800 years; a later quantitative study (Julian 2010, PhD diss., Univ. Manitoba) is reported (Wikipedia) to put Proto-Iroquoian c. 2624 BCE (~4570 BP) - not checked in original. No archaeological anchor.
source_original: Lounsbury 1961, Iroquois-Cherokee linguistic relations, in Fenton & Gulick (eds.) Symposium on Cherokee and Iroquois Culture, BAE Bulletin 180
source_dating_study: Julian 2010, A history of the Iroquoian languages (PhD, Univ. of Manitoba)

node_definition: MRCA of Mississippi Valley Siouan (Dakotan, Chiwere-Winnebago, Dhegiha)
event: ASJP calibration 'Mississippi Valley Siouan' = 2475 years
evidence_type: archaeology/inference (basis in Holman et al. not checked)
notes: Holman et al. value (years before c. 2000). ASJP 1725, GBD 1760, glottochronology 2404 (Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 5): both automated methods underestimate.
source_original: Holman et al. 2011, Automated dating of the world's language families based on lexical similarity, Current Anthropology 52(6):841-875 (calibration value as tabulated in Rama & Wichmann 2020 Table 1) 10.1086/662127
source_dating_study: Rama & Wichmann 2020, A test of Generalized Bayesian dating, PLOS ONE 15(8):e0236522 10.1371/journal.pone.0236522

node_definition: MRCA of Numic, Takic, Tubatulabal, Hopi (as subgroup recovered by Greenhill et al.)
event: Dispersal of Proto-Northern-Uto-Aztecan unlikely before earliest Mesquite (Prosopis) in the area, ~3490 BP (Fowler 1983; Hill 2015)
evidence_type: inference from reconstructed plant names + palaeobotany
notes: Greenhill et al. specify lognormal with mean 500 (real space), sigma 0.5, offset 2790; median 3230, 95% 2960-3970 (converted log-mean ln(500)-0.125=6.090). Their BP appears to be relative to c. 2000 CE (see MA-013). Note NUA monophyly itself is debated.
source_original: Fowler 1983, Some lexical clues to Uto-Aztecan prehistory, IJAL 49(3):224-257; Hill 2015
source_dating_study: Greenhill, Haynie, Ross, Chira, List, Campbell, Botero & Gray 2023, A recent northern origin for the Uto-Aztecan family, Language 99(1):81-107 (calibration section 2.3 of OSF preprint 10.31235/osf.io/k598j) 10.1353/lan.2023.0006

node_definition: MRCA of Takic (Serrano, Kitanemuk, Gabrielino/Tongva, Cupan: Cahuilla, Cupeno, Luiseno)
event: Population change c. 3000 BP (Sutton 2009); Takic arrival on southern Channel Islands 3000-2500 BP (Kerr 2004); shared fan-palm cognates, palms not in region before 2800 BP (Koehler & Anderson 1995)
notes: Greenhill et al.: lognormal mean 510 (real space), sigma 0.5, offset 2526; median 2980, 95% 2690-3730. Takic origins 'still under active debate'.
source_original: Sutton 2009; Kerr 2004; Koehler & Anderson 1995 (as cited in Greenhill et al. 2023)
source_dating_study: Greenhill, Haynie, Ross, Chira, List, Campbell, Botero & Gray 2023, A recent northern origin for the Uto-Aztecan family, Language 99(1):81-107 (calibration section 2.3 of OSF preprint 10.31235/osf.io/k598j) 10.1353/lan.2023.0006

node_definition: Tubatulabal node (varieties sampled by Greenhill et al.; single-language branch)
event: Continuous Tubatulabal occupation of Kern Plateau / Isabella Basin for 2500 years or longer (Garfinkel 2005)

node_definition: MRCA of Wati (Western Desert) languages, e.g. Pitjantjatjara, Ngaanyatjarra, Martu Wangka, Pintupi-Luritja, Kukatja
event: Expansion of Wati speakers into current Western Desert range; occupation from as early as ~5 ka to 1.5 ka, peak activity 3-2.5 ka
suggested_distribution: offset_lognormal_node(3000,6.37,0.64) + hard_minimum(1500)  [original: offset-gamma offset 3000, alpha=2, beta(scale)=359, 95% HPD 3000-5000, plus breakup no later than 1.5 ka]
notes: The ONLY node calibration in Bouckaert et al. 2018; the root age scales roughly linearly with it. Paper uses 'ka' before present, not stated as 1950-based (difference negligible). Archaeology dates occupation of the Western Desert, not the Wati split itself; linking is inferential. Other candidate calibrations (Queensland, Victoria, Lake Eyre Basin, offshore islands) were rejected as not linkable to nodes.
source_original: Veth/Smith Western Desert archaeology as cited (refs 13,74,75) in Bouckaert et al. 2018

Supports mid-Holocene rapid-replacement hypothesis over Pleistocene-origin hypotheses. | Demoted to C (2026-10-11, D1.2): the date is itself a lexical/Bayesian dating result, so it is circular as a calibration.

node_definition: Split between any Tasmanian language lineage and any mainland Australian lineage (only meaningful if a relationship is assumed)
event: Final flooding of the Bassian land bridge isolating Tasmania; last possible walking crossing at least 11,960 and likely ~12,425 years ago (Hamacher et al. 2023); older estimates ~14,000 BP for first major breach
notes: Bowern 2012 finds Tasmanian wordlists form ~5 clusters NOT demonstrably related to each other or to mainland languages, so this bound rarely attaches to a tree node. Ages are years before present (not explicitly 1950-based). Some sources give ~8,000 BP (outlier). Bound is 'split no later than' isolation.
source_original: Hamacher, Nunn, Gantevoort, Taylor, Lehman, Law & Miles 2023, The archaeology of orality: dating Tasmanian Aboriginal oral traditions to the Late Pleistocene, J Archaeol Sci

node_definition: MRCA of Tok Pisin, Bislama, Solomons Pijin

notes: CREOLE CAVEAT: not tree-like (lexifier English + Oceanic substrate, ongoing contact). Keesing 1988 argues stabilization already in the 1840s (~110 BP) from whaling/trade jargon and that Queensland and Samoan varieties were near-identical, against Muhlhausler's separate-development view. Tok Pisin glottocode from general knowledge.

node_definition: MRCA of Pitkern (Pitcairn) and Norfuk (Norfolk Island)

notes: CREOLE CAVEAT: English + Tahitian contact language; creole status contested. Back-migration 1858/1864 means post-split gene flow. Norfuk later influenced by Australian English. Very small populations: strong drift.

node_definition: MRCA of Sranan and Saramaccan (Saramaccan and Matawai from early Sranan/Dju-Tongo)
event: English colony 1651-1667 (max); Dutch takeover 1667; Portuguese-relexified 'Dju-Tongo' on Jewish plantations 1675-1680; first mass escapes forming the Saramaccan 1690-1695; Saramaccan structure fixed early 18th c.
notes: CREOLE CAVEAT: Saramaccan has heavy Portuguese and Gbe/Kikongo components, not a clean tree split. Britannica places Saramaccan crystallization in early 18th c., ApICS gives escapes 1690-1695.
source_original: Smith 1987, The genesis of the creole languages of Surinam (PhD, Amsterdam); Price 1983, First-Time
source_dating_study: Arends 2017, Language and Slavery: a social and linguistic history of the Suriname creoles, Benjamins (CLL 52); ApICS survey 3 (Saramaccan) 10.1075/cll.52

node_definition: MRCA of Sranan and Ndyuka (Eastern Maroon Creole)

node_definition: MRCA of Quebec French and metropolitan French
event: Quebec City founded 1608; French immigration mostly 1608-1760; British conquest 1760/Treaty of Paris 1763 ends French settler inflow
notes: Settler founders mainly from NW France (koine formation in 17th c.); ongoing standard-French influence. Acadian (Port-Royal 1605) is a separate branch.
source_original: Standard historical record

node_definition: MRCA of American and British English varieties
event: Jamestown 1607, Plymouth 1620; independence 1776
notes: Continuous contact, migration and print standardization; colonial lag hypotheses; usable only as weak max bound or benchmark of near-zero lexical divergence.
source_original: Standard historical record

node_definition: Cape Verdean Creole (all varieties: Sotavento incl. Santiago; Barlavento incl. Sao Vicente)
event: Settlement of Santiago (Ribeira Grande) from 1462 (max for creole); later settlement of Barlavento islands (Sao Vicente mostly late 18th-19th c.) for Sotavento/Barlavento split
notes: Santiago 1462 from general knowledge, not re-verified this session; Barlavento-Sotavento split dates not verified (grade for that sub-claim U). CREOLE CAVEAT; relationship to Guinea-Bissau Kriyol (Upper Guinea Creole) also relevant.
source_original: to verify (e.g. Baptista; ApICS Cape Verdean surveys)
